baseline_acceptance.reason: The durable production rows and source bytes are unchanged since v5; v7, like v6, builds on that same snapshot.

supersedes.reason: v6 recorded the selector-identity fix but kept the hard FPP/confidence eligibility gate that made follow-up selection return zero targets; v7 corrects that selection semantics defect. v6 remains valid historical evidence and is not modified.

corrected_defect.summary: create_search() hard-failed and created no search whenever fewer candidates than requested passed the follow-up scientific quality gate (FPP<0.15, confidence>0.40, eligible pathway), instead of returning the best available N with quality reported separately.
corrected_defect.prior_framing: v3-v6 all recorded 'zero eligible from 202 evaluated, no search created' as the scientifically correct outcome. Given the current business requirement that a normal top-N request must return the best available N and never fail purely because none clear a quality bar, that framing was itself the defect, not a valid terminal state.
corrected_defect.fix: eligibility is now availability (not already scheduled/completed/deferred, and an unfollowed candidate_found signal exists); the FPP/confidence/pathway gate is reported per-candidate as meets_strict_follow_up_bar instead of removing candidates from the selectable pool. create_search() only raises when zero candidates are available at all.

new.eligibility: novel target; strict ASAS-SN exclusion; advanced to metadata stage; at least one QLP product

follow-up.selection_semantics: rank by priority across every currently available (non-duplicate, data-confirmed) follow-up candidate; return the best available N even when fewer than N clear the strict production bar below

live_business_validation.method: HunterStore API invoked directly (same code path Create-New-Search uses) against a disposable local copy of the real production database data/hunter_searches.sqlite3; the real file was never mutated, and the disposable copy was deleted after the probe.

follow_up_universe_before_fix.source: artifacts/manifests/hunter_live_acceptance_v4.json and v6.json, both recording zero eligible targets under the old hard FPP/confidence gate

follow_up_universe_after_fix.interpretation: All 190 unfollowed candidate_found signals in the real durable history are below the strict FPP<0.15/confidence>0.40/pathway bar, which is why v3-v6 saw zero eligible targets under the old hard-gate design. They are nonetheless real, ranked, previously-invisible follow-up candidates.

live_business_validation.not_yet_demonstrated_live: The 'new' mode shortfall path (create_search never hard-failing when fewer than N new candidates are available) is covered by focused unit/integration tests against synthetic pools, not a live MAST sweep exhaustion, since the current default pool sizing (>=10,000 candidates for typical N) has not been observed to run dry against the live TIC catalog.

verification.quality_gate_result: 10/10 gates passed in 26.1 seconds under the canonical 6x6 topology

remaining_limitations: The strict production bar (FPP<0.15, confidence>0.40, eligible pathway) is unchanged as a scientific quality signal; it is now reported per-candidate rather than used to silently remove candidates from the selectable pool.
The selector weights are conservative versioned project policy, not a claim of a universally optimal scientific ranking.
Live archive/catalog inputs can change; reproducibility attaches to the frozen candidate snapshot and contract.

New-mode adaptive discovery expansion (widening the search when the live sweep itself returns fewer raw candidates than requested) is not yet implemented; current default pool sizing makes this rare but not impossible as the exclusion set grows with repeated real usage.
No external submission, alert, confirmation, or discovery claim is authorized.
